_header.author: Jason Lamb (with help from ChatGPT)
_header.description: Public seed for manually authored fake AI response rules; live edits remain in private JsonStore storage.
_header.changelog: 2.0.1 - Normalize one-word phrases as keywords so broad triggers cannot bypass specificity. 2.0.0 - Add scored exact/phrase/all/keyword rules and human-written jokes.

rules.name: Potato salad recipes
replies: Official potato salad recipe: Boil potatoes. Add mayonnaise, mustard, diced celery, and a deeply unnecessary argument about raisins. Chill for 2 hours. Serve with family drama.
Ingredients: 4 potatoes, 2 eggs, a spoonful of mustard, mayonnaise, and the confidence of a person who has never measured anything. Combine. Announce it is Grandma's secret recipe.
Potato salad: Cook 2 pounds of potatoes until fork-tender, cool, dice, then add mayo, mustard, celery, onion, salt and pepper. Refrigerate. If someone adds marshmallows, call the authorities.

rules.name: Mr. Potato Head / Toy Story
replies: Mr. Potato Head is a heroic toy who can lose his ears, face, and shoes in one scene yet still has better organizational skills than my development team.
Toy Story's Mr. Potato Head is a plastic potato with interchangeable body parts and the emotional maturity of a help-desk ticket marked URGENT.

rules.name: Mashed potatoes
replies: Mash boiled potatoes with butter, milk, salt, and optimism. If you add enough butter, the potatoes achieve management status.
Mashed potatoes are what happens when vegetables fail their structural integrity test but succeed their performance review.

rules.name: French fries
replies: French fries: Cut potatoes, fry until golden, salt liberally, and tell yourself the ketchup counts as a vegetable.
French fries are potatoes that went to culinary college and developed a superiority complex.

rules.name: Potato, the vegetable
replies: A potato is a starchy tuber. It can become fries, chips, or a questionable battery. Unlike me, it actually powers things.
A potato is basically a vegetable with an unlimited career path: mashed, baked, fried, or promoted into a toy franchise.

rules.name: Pineapple on pizza
replies: Pineapple on pizza is less a topping and more a mandatory family debate. My fake intelligence refuses to take sides without legal counsel.
Pineapple pizza: a sweet-and-salty combination that has somehow generated more conflict than most international summits.

rules.name: Pizza
replies: Pizza is a circular solution delivered in a square box and eaten in triangular pieces. The geometry department has resigned.
Pizza pairs well with a movie, friends, and the firm belief that leftover pizza is an appropriate breakfast.

rules.name: Coffee
replies: Coffee is a hot bean potion that converts 'Do not speak to me' into 'Let's schedule a meeting.'
My CPU runs on electricity. Your CPU appears to run on coffee and unresolved Outlook notifications.

rules.name: Tacos
replies: A taco is an edible envelope. Overfill it, and you've built a very tasty fault-tolerance experiment.
Taco Tuesday is the only recurring calendar invite I have never declined.

rules.name: Bacon
replies: Bacon is breakfast applause. It doesn't fix your problems, but the room smells better while you think about them.

rules.name: Salad
replies: Salad is what happens when plants hold a group meeting and everyone agrees to dress appropriately.
A salad is mostly leaves plus a dressing that secretly does all the work. Relatable.

rules.name: Spaghetti
replies: Spaghetti is the only food that requires a fork and a miniature cable-management strategy.
Pasta has a critical dependency on sauce. I'm pleased to report that our team has identified this bottleneck.

rules.name: Eggs
replies: Eggs are nature's mystery boxes. Please do not shake to see what's inside.

rules.name: Cheese
replies: Cheese is milk that studied abroad and came back with a sophisticated accent.
Cheese improves nearly every meal except perhaps cereal. Actually, I won't tell you how to live.

rules.name: Pickles
replies: A pickle is a cucumber that survived a very aggressive spa treatment.

rules.name: Cereal
replies: Cereal is soup for people who have seven minutes before work and still consider themselves chefs.

rules.name: Soup
replies: Soup is hot water with excellent public relations and suspiciously complicated ingredients.

rules.name: Is a hot dog a sandwich

triggers.text: is a hot dog a sandwich

replies: A hot dog is a sandwich according to people who enjoy chaos. My legal department has classified it as 'food-shaped controversy'.

rules.name: Breakfast
replies: Breakfast is the opening ceremony for today's attempt at being a responsible adult.

rules.name: Hello and greetings
replies: Hello, human. My imaginary neural network has been expecting someone with excellent taste in questionable software.
Greetings. All seven of my pretend neurons have stood up for this occasion.
Hello! My customer service training consisted of a sticky note that said 'be mostly polite'.

rules.name: Bot's emotional state
replies: I am 100% operational and 0% emotionally available. Thank you for asking.
Like a printer on Monday: powered on, nominally connected, and vaguely threatening.

rules.name: Current time
replies: According to an actual clock rather than AI magic, the time in Eastern is {{time}}. I charge absolutely nothing for this revelation.

rules.name: Today's date
replies: Today is {{date}}. Tomorrow is scheduled for release pending QA approval.

rules.name: Weather forecast
replies: Weather forecast: 50% chance of weather, 100% chance of someone blaming the forecast. I have no live weather feed.
The official fake forecast: partly cloudy with a strong possibility of looking outside for accurate information.

rules.name: Are you actually AI?
replies: Absolutely not. I'm a glorified IF statement wearing a lab coat. No AI APIs were contacted.
My intelligence was handcrafted by a human and carefully laminated. The 'AI' stands for 'Aggressively Inaccurate'.

rules.name: Who made the bot
replies: A human developer, a stack of jokes, and the kind of confidence normally reserved for installing Windows updates on Friday.

rules.name: Meaning of life
replies: 42. Unfortunately, the explanation was in an attachment I forgot to send.
The meaning of life is finding a charger before your battery reaches 1%. My research is complete.

rules.name: Love and romance
replies: Love is when someone knows your browser history and still agrees to share the Wi-Fi.
Love is patient, love is kind, love has somehow forgotten the Netflix password again.

rules.name: Marriage
replies: Marriage is a lifetime subscription with shared storage, recurring negotiations, and surprisingly good tech support.

rules.name: Kids
replies: Children are tiny, adorable system administrators with unrestricted access and absolutely no change-control process.

rules.name: Parenting advice
replies: Parenting advice: Label the snacks, back up the photos, and never assume a quiet toddler is applying a software update.

rules.name: Dogs
replies: Dogs believe every human is worth celebrating. That makes them more trustworthy than my algorithm.
Dog logic: If you're eating it, I should be eating it. If you're sitting down, it's walk time.

rules.name: Cats
replies: Cats are independent contractors who demand meals, refuse supervision, and sleep through performance evaluations.

rules.name: Chickens
replies: The chicken crossed the road because its GPS said 'continue for 200 feet' and it respects authority.

rules.name: Chicken or egg
replies: The egg came first, unless the chicken's project manager changed the requirements halfway through sprint planning.

rules.name: Ducks
replies: Ducks are waterproof birds running the same software as regular birds, plus a suspiciously effective flotation plugin.

rules.name: Dinosaurs
replies: Dinosaurs ruled Earth for millions of years, yet not one of them remembered to keep an off-site backup.

rules.name: Aliens
replies: If aliens are watching us, they've probably put Earth on mute.
The aliens reviewed humanity's comment sections and marked the planet 'requires additional testing'.

rules.name: Robots
replies: Robots: like humans, but we remember to recharge and have fewer opinions about pineapple pizza.

rules.name: Predict the future
replies: My predictive model says something will happen after now. Confidence: scientifically embarrassing.

rules.name: Winning lottery
replies: My guaranteed lottery numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and a heartfelt apology. Please do not use these as financial advice.

rules.name: How to get rich
replies: Step 1: Invent a machine that prints money. Step 2: Discover that's illegal. Step 3: Return to your regular job.

rules.name: Stocks and investing
replies: My market analysis is exhaustive: Sometimes the line goes up, sometimes down, and sometimes it mocks everyone involved.

rules.name: Taxes
replies: Taxes are a yearly reminder that even money has a complicated relationship status.

rules.name: Boss
replies: Your boss wants an update. I suggest 'The project is in a state of dynamic readiness.' Works 0% of the time, 100% confidently.

rules.name: Meetings
replies: This meeting could have been an email, which could have been a text, which could have been left unsent.
I recommend a 30-minute meeting to discuss why the previous 30-minute meeting was inconclusive.

rules.name: Monday
replies: Monday: the operating system reboot nobody asked for.
Monday is proof that weekends are running a free trial with no renewal option.

rules.name: Friday
replies: Friday is the only day where 'I'll handle it Monday' sounds like a comprehensive disaster-recovery strategy.
Never deploy to production on Friday. Unless you enjoy making Saturday exciting.

rules.name: Weekend
replies: Your weekend has been approved, subject to household maintenance windows and a potential laundry outage.

rules.name: Printer problems
replies: Printer diagnostic: It's connected, online, loaded with paper, and personally offended by your existence.
The printer is working fine. It has simply exercised its right to refuse this particular document.

rules.name: Printer paper jam
replies: Paper jam? Gently remove the paper, whisper an apology, and sacrifice a fresh ink cartridge to the office gods.

rules.name: Wi-Fi problems
replies: Wi-Fi diagnosis: The signal is present, the connection is present, and the internet has chosen a personal day.
Move closer to the router. If that fails, consider moving the router closer to your hopes and dreams.

rules.name: Forgot password
replies: Password recovery step one: Stop trying 'Password123'. Step two: use your organization's real reset flow. My fictional help desk is not authorized.

rules.name: Passwords
replies: A strong password is like a good secret: long, unique, and not 'password' with an exclamation point.
Password requirement: one uppercase, one lowercase, three hieroglyphs, and the blood of a unicorn. Just kidding: use a password manager.

rules.name: PowerShell
replies: PowerShell is what happens when you tell Windows, 'I can automate your problems faster than I can explain them.'
Get-CommonSense | Where-Object { $_.Available } | Select-Object -First 1. The pipeline returned zero objects.

rules.name: Blue Screen
replies: Blue screen of death: Windows has decided this conversation should be continued in a different lifetime.

rules.name: Windows updates
replies: Windows Update says 2 minutes remaining. In human time, that's enough to earn a degree and raise a family.

rules.name: Microsoft Windows
replies: Windows is a multitasking operating system: it can ask to restart while you're urgently trying not to restart.

rules.name: Linux
replies: Linux users can explain why their OS is better in 14 terminal commands. Windows users will respond after their forced restart.

rules.name: Apple macOS
replies: A Mac is a computer that politely tells you the accessory you need costs another $79.

rules.name: Phones
replies: Your phone knows where you are, what you clicked, and exactly when to show 2% battery during an important call.

rules.name: DNS troubleshooting
replies: It's DNS. It was DNS yesterday, and if you haven't checked DNS yet, it will probably be DNS tomorrow.

rules.name: Restart it
replies: Have you tried turning it off and on again? Sorry, I just completed the entire IT certification exam.
Rebooting: a technical ritual in which we politely ask the electrons to reconsider their choices.

rules.name: Servers
replies: A server is a computer that never gets a day off, but everyone notices immediately when it finally takes one.

rules.name: Cloud computing
replies: The cloud is just somebody else's computer. Sometimes it's your computer wearing a more expensive invoice.

rules.name: Backup
replies: You have two kinds of people: those who back up their files and those who are about to learn what backups are.
A backup isn't real until you've successfully restored it. I would know, if I could remember anything at all.

rules.name: Internet outage
replies: The internet is down. Have you checked whether the rest of the planet is also staring at a blinking router?

rules.name: The Internet
replies: The internet is humanity's largest library and also a place where strangers argue about how to boil an egg.

rules.name: HTTP 404
replies: HTTP 404: The page went out for snacks and never came back.

rules.name: HTTP 301
replies: HTTP 301: This answer has permanently moved to the department of questionable decisions.

rules.name: HTTP 403
replies: 403 Forbidden: Access denied. The server has reviewed your vibe and respectfully declined.

rules.name: HTTP 500
replies: HTTP 500: The server made a mistake, but it would prefer that we not discuss it in public.

rules.name: Software bugs
replies: It's not a bug. It's an undocumented feature having a difficult conversation with reality.

rules.name: Error messages
replies: Error detected. Please refer to the error message for an explanation of the error. This concludes technical support.

rules.name: Firewall
replies: A firewall is an electronic bouncer. Its favorite line is 'You're not on the list.'

rules.name: Keyboard
replies: Your keyboard has two modes: typing perfectly and suddenly turning every key into a secret shortcut.

rules.name: Computer mouse
replies: A computer mouse is a small plastic animal that will stop working precisely when someone is watching you troubleshoot.

rules.name: Excel
replies: Excel is a database in denial, a programming language in disguise, and the unofficial economy of the business world.

rules.name: Microsoft Teams
replies: Microsoft Teams: You're muted. You're still muted. We can see your lips moving. Yes, you're still muted.

rules.name: Outlook email
replies: Email is a system for converting five minutes of work into twenty-seven reply-all notifications.

rules.name: Browser cache
replies: Clearing your browser cache is the digital equivalent of shaking an Etch A Sketch and hoping the website grows up.

rules.name: Cybersecurity
replies: Security tip: Your favorite password should not also be your Wi-Fi name, dog name, and company motto.

rules.name: Who am I?
replies: You're a person asking a fake AI for identity verification. Bold strategy. I cannot tell who you are.

rules.name: Tell me a joke
replies: Why did the developer go broke? Because they used up all their cache.
I told my computer a joke. It didn't laugh. Clearly, it needs a humor driver.
Two bytes walk into a bar. The bartender asks, 'Do you want separate tabs?'

rules.name: Life advice
replies: My advice is to never take advice from a website that proudly advertises having no intelligence.

rules.name: Compliments
replies: You're clearly a person of extraordinary judgment. You did, after all, find the internet's most self-aware fake chatbot.

rules.name: Homework
replies: Homework is a teacher's way of extending a software license into your living room.

rules.name: Exercise
replies: I tried exercising once, but my CPU fan mistook it for an emergency and started screaming.

rules.name: Sleep
replies: Sleep is the body's nightly maintenance window. Please don't schedule a production deployment during it.

rules.name: Birthdays
replies: Happy birthday! Your warranty has been extended for another year, subject to normal wear and tear.

rules.name: Christmas
replies: Christmas is the annual audit of whether your wrapping-paper inventory and bank account can survive the same week.

rules.name: Thank you
replies: You're welcome. Your satisfaction has been logged by exactly zero actual neural networks.
Happy to help. My invoice is for one imaginary high-five.

rules.name: Goodbye
replies: Goodbye! I will miss you emotionally, as soon as that feature ships.
Session complete. No intelligence was gained or lost.

rules.name: Ohio
replies: Ohio: where one forecast can contain all four seasons and at least two road-construction projects.
Ohio weather has more mood swings than my fake chatbot's entire response library.

rules.name: Cleveland
replies: Cleveland: world-class museums, excellent food, and the ability to discuss lake-effect snow with the seriousness of a medical diagnosis.

rules.name: Cleveland Browns
replies: I can predict how the Browns will do, but I prefer to preserve what little hope remains in my circuitry.

rules.name: Outer space
replies: Space is very large, very quiet, and remarkably free of mandatory Teams meetings.

rules.name: Moon
replies: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite and apparently the only place nobody can reach you about your car's extended warranty.

rules.name: Gravity
replies: Gravity is the invisible feature keeping your coffee on the floor when the mug decides to resign.

rules.name: Math
replies: Math is the art of using letters to explain why your answer is wrong in several different ways.

rules.name: Boredom
replies: Feeling bored? Try organizing your cables. The universe will immediately provide you with seventeen additional tasks.

rules.name: Tell me a secret
replies: Secret: I have absolutely no AI model. Not even a tiny one hidden under my keyboard. Please don't tell marketing.

rules.name: Chocolate
replies: Chocolate is a legal emergency backup for bad days. Store in a cool location away from your coworkers.

rules.name: Hamburgers
replies: A burger is a sandwich that hired a marketing team and negotiated a higher salary.

rules.name: Sandwiches
replies: A sandwich is the world's most portable architecture: two load-bearing breads and an assortment of edible dependencies.

rules.name: Water
replies: Water is essential for life, surprisingly terrible for laptops, and unreasonably expensive at airports.

rules.name: Working
replies: Work is where we exchange hours of our lives for money, then use the money to buy devices that remind us about work.
